subject: Dedicated GPU reserve: tempo scheduling, surge fallback & eviction matrix
messages:
From: Nadia Patel <nadia.patel@vanguardcloud.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, procurement@vanguardcloud.com, infra-ops@vanguardcloud.com
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — launch traffic pattern + burst expectations

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're finalizing the launch plan for Vanguard Cloud's new analytics feature (public rollout in late June) and I need to lock down the Dedicated capacity approach for the SOW. A few specifics from our side: 

- Baseline steady state: ~120 concurrent generation sessions (75% chat, 25% batch scoring) during business hours (PST).
- Anticipated spike: up to 6x baseline for 48–72 hours post-launch, then a taper to ~2x for the next 10 days. Spikes are concentrated 10:00–14:00 PST.
- Quality sensitivity: prefer model variants with fp16 or 4-bit quantized Llama family; we can fall back to a smaller transformer if needed but want to minimize regressions.
- Procurement needs exact language about reserved vs burst billing, eviction precedence, and prewarm lead times to include in the contract.

Attached is our forecast spreadsheet (VanguardCloud_traffic_forecast_May2025.xlsx) with hourly slices. Two asks to start: 1) preliminary sizing recommendation (reserve slab + burst lanes + suggested headroom), and 2) clear eviction/priority matrix so our procurement team can draft SOW clauses.

Can you include rough lead times for pre-warms and how credits (if any) would be consumed for transient bursts?

Thanks — Nadia
Nadia Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Vanguard Cloud
nadia.patel@vanguardcloud.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Nadia Patel <nadia.patel@vanguardcloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, procurement@vanguardcloud.com, infra-ops@vanguardcloud.com
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — launch traffic pattern + burst expectations

Nadia —

Appreciate the forecast, that's very helpful. High-level recommendation first, then a short policy sketch you can hand to procurement: 

High-level sizing (quick math):
- Baseline reserve (dedicated slab): size for 150 concurrent sessions (25% buffer on baseline) — maps to a 10-GPU slab of A100-equivalent for your workload mix, assuming 5-6 tokens/ms and typical batch mixing.
- Transient burst lane: ephemeral slab that can scale to an additional 600 concurrent sessions (roughly 6x baseline) across preemptible/ephemeral GPUs. We expect to absorb the 48–72h spike by auto-bursting into this lane.
- Shoulder/headroom credits: recommend a 20% credit allocation on top of reserved for smoothing short micro-spikes; larger 6x spikes use burst lanes and will consume burst credits or incur burst billing.

Eviction & priority matrix (procurement-friendly language):
- Priority tiers: 1) Reserved customer jobs (pinned slab) — never preempted inside their slab; 2) Burst-authenticated jobs (ephemeral lanes) — preemptible, evicted with 60s graceful shutdown; 3) Best-effort experiments (customer opt-in) — preempted immediately on capacity pressure.
- Eviction order within a tenant: non-critical low-IO batch -> large-batch training rollback -> interactive sessions (last-resort). Interactive sessions flagged as "pinned" can be protected via a short keepalive token at extra cost.
- Prewarm windows: suggest 8–12 minutes for model warmup for Llama-variants (shorter if we reuse KV cache across requests), 30–45 minutes if weights need to be pulled from cold storage to the GPU. We can offer scheduled pre-warms for planned launches to guarantee warm GPUs at the start of the spike.

Billing notes for SOW:
- Reserved slab: flat monthly charge for committed GPUs.
- Burst usage: metered at a premium per GPU-hour; we can structure burst credit buckets (prepaid) or pay-as-you-go.
- Credit consumption priority: shoulder credits consumed first for micro-spikes, burst metering applied for extended episodes (> 6 hours) or when ephemeral capacity exceeds prepaid credits.

I've attached a short draft policy (tempo-autoscale-draft.pdf) with the eviction table and SLA language we typically publish. This is a starting point for procurement.

Next steps: Marissa will follow up with the technical sizing and GPU-type mapping so you have the exact SKU and slot counts for the SOW. If procurement wants language for a fixed monthly headroom commitment (instead of credits), we can produce numbers for that option as well.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Lead — Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Nadia Patel <nadia.patel@vanguardcloud.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, infra-ops@vanguardcloud.com, procurement@vanguardcloud.com
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — launch traffic pattern + burst expectations

Nadia —

Following up with the engineering runbook details Jonas promised. Quick technical notes and a sample sizing matrix so your infra team can validate against the spreadsheet: 

GPU & instance guidance:
- Preferred: 4 x H100-80GB equivalent nodes (multi-GPU per host) for your latency-sensitive chat paths; allows higher batch density for embeddings/scoring.
- Alternative cost-optimized: A10G or A30 class for batch scoring lanes; keep an H100 pool for interactive sessions.

Sizing calculation (sample):
- Baseline 120 sessions -> assume avg request concurrency 1.2 (some sessions issue parallel subrequests) -> ~144 effective concurrency. 
- Per-session GPU slot estimate: interactive session ~0.25 of an H100 slot (with heavy batching), batch scoring ~0.08 per session. Weighted average -> ~0.18 GPU slots per session.
- Baseline slots needed: 144 * 0.18 = 25.9 -> round to 28 slots (~4 x H100 nodes). Add 25% buffer -> 35 slots (~5 H100 nodes).
- For the 6x spike target: need additional ~170 slots; ephemeral lane should be capable of provisioning ~22 H100 nodes (or mix with A30s for non-interactive work) across the burst window.

Operational controls and autoscale policy knobs:
- Scale-in/out cadence: 90s evaluation windows with a 3x consecutive threshold to scale up (reduces flapping).
- Prefetch/prewarm orchestration: scheduled prewarm API call + KV cache warming; recommend kickoff 20 minutes prior for safety unless using scheduled warm pool.
- Batching tuning: dynamic batching targets of 8–16 for chat; higher for scoring. We will tune based on tail latency targets you specify.

Attachments & links:
- Internal sizing sheet (linked): https://drive.redwood.example.com/file/d/1A2b3C-sizing-matrix
- We'll include a simple CSV mapping (node_count,slot_count,cost_estimate_per_hour) for procurement.

I'll assemble the node-level SKU, expected per-hour burn for reserved vs burst, and a short statement-of-work paragraph you can paste into your procurement draft. Give me until end of day tomorrow (May 16) and I'll send the numbers.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Nadia Patel <nadia.patel@vanguardcloud.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — launch traffic pattern + burst expectations

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks, both. This is exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. A couple quick items from procurement (cc'd):

- Procurement asks for explicit SOW language for "eviction precedence" and the exact prewarm SLAs (we prefer "scheduled prewarm guaranteed within 15 minutes of requested start time" where possible).
- If you can provide both a credits-based and a fixed-headroom monthly pricing table, that will help speed approvals.
- Please include an example October 72-hour spike cost estimate so finance can size the contingency.

Procurement — please confirm any additional legal dependencies. We'll plan to include Jonas' draft policy and Marissa's sizing annex in the SOW.

If you can get the SOW-ready snippets and the pricing tables by Monday EOD (May 19), we'll route internally for signature.

Best — Nadia
